title: Take your career to Germany with the Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte)
summary: The Germany Opportunity Card lets skilled workers job-hunt in Germany for a year. Points, eligibility and documents in one guide. Apply with confidence.
body_markdown:
Moving to Germany might have been on your mind for a while. You've probably browsed job listings, researched cities and wondered how much you would need to save. But finding a German employer willing to hire you while you're still in Nigeria can be one of the biggest challenges.


So what if you could move to Germany first and look for a job once you're there?


The Germany Opportunity Card, also known as the Chancenkarte, is a residence permit that allows qualified non-EU nationals to live in Germany for up to one year while looking for work. Applicants can qualify through recognised professional or academic qualifications or by meeting the requirements of a points-based system.


In this guide, I'll explore who qualifies, how to calculate your points, how to apply from Nigeria and how much money you'll need to prepare for the move.


## What is the Chancenkarte?


The Chancenkarte is a German job-seeking residence permit that allows skilled workers from outside the EU to enter Germany without having a job offer.


Introduced in June 2024 as part of Germany's Skilled Immigration Act, the Opportunity Card was designed to attract international talent and address labour shortages.


For Nigerian professionals, this means you can attend interviews in person, meet potential employers and explore career opportunities while living in Germany.


With the Opportunity Card, you can:


- Stay in Germany for up to 12 months to search for employment.
- Work part-time for up to 20 hours per week in total.
- Participate in work trials for up to two weeks per employer, subject to applicable conditions.
- Apply for an appropriate work residence permit once you secure qualifying employment.


Keep in mind that the Opportunity Card doesn't guarantee employment or permanent residency. It gives you time and permission to find a suitable job.


## How does the Germany Opportunity Card points system work?


You need at least six points to qualify for the Opportunity Card through the points system. However, if your academic or professional qualifications are already fully recognised in Germany, you can apply without collecting points.


For everyone applying through the points system, factors such as professional experience, qualifications, language skills and age determine your score.


According to Germany's official[Make it in Germany portal](https://www.make-it-in-germany.com/en/visa-recognition/opportunity-card/job-search) , this is how points are awarded:


Eligibility criteria Points


Partial recognition of professional qualifications in Germany 4


Qualification in a shortage occupation 1


Five years of relevant work experience within the past seven years 3


Two years of relevant work experience within the past five years 2


German language skills at B2 or above 3


German language skills at B1 2


German language skills at A2 1


English language skills at C1 or above, or native proficiency 1


Under 35 years old 2


Between 35 and 40 years old, excluding 40 1


Previous qualifying stay in Germany of at least six consecutive months within the past five years 1


Accompanying spouse or registered partner who qualifies for the Opportunity Card 1


Minimum required score 6


Points within the same age, German language, and work experience categories cannot be combined. English-language points can be earned in addition to German-language points.


### Example: How to calculate your Opportunity Card points


Imagine you're a 29-year-old Nigerian software developer with a university degree recognised in Nigeria, four years of relevant professional experience and certified English and German language skills.


You've reached the six-point threshold without ever having lived in Germany or received a job offer.


If you're a few points short, it is time to sign up to a few classes and work on your German language skills. Obtaining formal recognition of your qualifications could help you qualify in the future.


## Who is eligible for the Germany Opportunity Card?


Nigerian citizens with suitable academic or vocational qualifications, sufficient financial resources and the relevant recognition or points requirements can apply for the Opportunity Card.


There are two routes to eligibility.


### Option 1: Apply with fully recognised qualifications


If your university degree or vocational qualification is fully recognised in Germany, you can apply as a skilled worker without going through the points system.


You don't need to demonstrate a minimum language level for this route, although speaking German can significantly improve your employment prospects.


### Option 2: Apply through the points system


If your qualifications are not fully recognised in Germany, you must meet the following requirements:


- Have a university degree or a qualifying vocational qualification recognised in the country where you obtained it.
- Have completed at least two years of training if applying with a vocational qualification.
- Demonstrate German proficiency at A1 level or English proficiency at B2 level or higher.
- Achieve at least six points.


Both routes require proof that you can financially support yourself during your stay.


As of 2026, the minimum financial requirement is €1,091 per month, equivalent to €13,092 for a full year if you are financing your entire stay through a blocked account.


### Can Nigerians apply without speaking German?


Yes, you can qualify through the points system with sufficient English proficiency, even if you don't speak German.


However, don't assume that being Nigerian or completing your university education in English automatically exempts you from language certification. You may need an accepted certificate, such as IELTS or TOEFL.


Even if German isn't required for your application, learning some before moving can make everything from apartment hunting to job interviews much easier.


## How to apply for the Germany Opportunity Card from Nigeria


You can apply for the Germany Opportunity Card online through the German Federal Foreign Office's Consular Services Portal. Here's how the process works.


### Step 1: Check your eligibility


Start by finding out which of the two application routes applies to you.


Check the recognition status of your qualifications and, if necessary, calculate your points. Do this before spending money on language examinations, document preparation or application fees.


### Step 2: Get your qualifications assessed


If you studied at a Nigerian university, you can check your institution and degree through Germany's Anabin database.


Depending on the results, you may need a Statement of Comparability from the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB).


Applicants with vocational qualifications may require a Digital Statement on Professional Qualification or other recognition documents.


Give yourself enough time for this stage, particularly if your qualifications require an individual assessment.


### Step 3: Gather your documents


The German missions in Nigeria have specific documentation requirements for Opportunity Card applicants.


Your checklist will generally include the following:


You'll also need to prepare:


- Completed visa application and required declarations.
- CV outlining your education and professional experience.
- Signed motivation letter explaining your plans in Germany.
- Evidence of job applications or correspondence with German employers.
- Employment references and supporting documents for any points claimed.
- Birth certificate, academic transcripts and relevant civil records.
- Biometric passport photographs and a prepaid courier envelope.


Check the complete[Opportunity Card application checklist for Nigeria](https://nigeria.diplo.de/ng-en/2750760-2750760) before submitting your application. You may also need to arrange appropriate health insurance before travelling.


### Step 4: Arrange your proof of funds


You'll have to prepare evidence that you can cover your living expenses in Germany through a blocked account, eligible part-time employment or a formal declaration of commitment.


If you're relying on savings, remember to account for exchange rate fluctuations when converting your naira into euros.


### Step 5: Submit your application online


Create an account on the Consular Services Portal, complete your application and upload the required documents.


Your application will undergo a preliminary review before you receive instructions for scheduling an in-person appointment.


### Step 6: Attend your visa appointment


Bring your original documents and the required copies to your appointment at the relevant German mission.


You'll provide biometric information, attend an interview and pay the visa application fee, which is generally €75 or its equivalent in local currency.


### Step 7: Wait for a decision


Processing times vary depending on appointment availability, application volumes and the complexity of your case.


It's worth starting the process several months before your intended departure, especially if you still need to get your qualifications assessed.


Avoid booking non-refundable flights or accommodation until your visa has been approved.


## What happens after you arrive in Germany?


Once you arrive, you can start looking for qualified employment, work within the permitted part-time limits and apply for a different residence permit when you secure a suitable job.


But before diving into job applications, there are a few practical things to organise, including registering your address, arranging health insurance and setting up access to your money.


### Finding a job in Germany


You don't have to wait until you arrive to start applying for jobs. In fact, building a list of potential employers while you're still in Nigeria could save you valuable time and money.


Platforms such as LinkedIn, StepStone, Indeed Germany and the Federal Employment Agency's job portal are useful starting points.


You can also explore[German companies that sponsor work visas](https://grey.co/blog/germany-companies-sponsor-work-visa) to identify employers familiar with international recruitment.


Consider looking beyond Berlin and Munich, too. Smaller cities may offer interesting career opportunities alongside more affordable accommodation.


### Switching to a German work permit


Once you receive a qualifying job offer, you can apply for an appropriate employment residence permit through the local immigration authority.


Depending on your qualifications, occupation and salary, your options may include:


- A work visa for qualified professionals.
- A residence permit for professionally experienced workers.
- [The EU Blue Card route](https://grey.co/blog/eu-blue-card-guide) .
- A residence permit for qualification recognition.


In certain circumstances, the Opportunity Card can also be extended for up to two additional years if you have secured qualified employment but cannot obtain another eligible employment residence permit.


Make sure you apply before your current permit expires and obtain the necessary authorisation before starting work beyond the Opportunity Card's permitted limits.


## Proving funds and sending money to Germany


Moving from Nigeria to Germany involves more than paying for your visa and booking a flight. You'll need enough money to support yourself while searching for employment, particularly during those first few months.


### How much money do you need for the Opportunity Card?


The financial requirement for 2026 is €1,091 for each month of your planned stay.


Length of stay Required financial proof


3 months €3,273


6 months €6,546


9 months €9,819


12 months €13,092


*These figures assume you are covering the full financial requirement through savings.*


Remember that the required amount is an immigration threshold, not necessarily a realistic budget for every German city. Flights, rental deposits, insurance and initial relocation expenses can add considerably to your costs.


### What is a blocked account in Germany?


A blocked account, known in Germany as a Sperrkonto, is a special bank account used to demonstrate that you have sufficient funds to support yourself.


You deposit the required amount before moving to Germany. Once you arrive and activate the account, you can access your money in monthly instalments rather than withdrawing the entire balance at once.


Other accepted ways to demonstrate financial resources may include a formal declaration of commitment from an eligible sponsor or a qualifying part-time employment contract.


If your part-time earnings don't cover the monthly requirement, you may be able to cover the difference through a blocked account.

## Frequently asked questions about the Germany Opportunity Card


### What is the Germany Opportunity Card?


The Germany Opportunity Card, or Chancenkarte, is a residence permit that allows eligible non-EU nationals to live in Germany for up to one year while looking for qualified employment, without needing a job offer before travelling.


### How many points do I need for the Germany Opportunity Card?


You need a minimum of six points if applying through the points-based route. Applicants with qualifications fully recognised in Germany can qualify without meeting the points threshold.


### Who qualifies for the Germany Opportunity Card?


Qualified non-EU nationals, including Nigerians, can apply if they meet the applicable academic or vocational qualification, financial and recognition requirements. Those applying through the points system must also meet the minimum language requirement and score at least six points.


### How long is the Germany Opportunity Card valid?


The initial Opportunity Card is valid for up to 12 months, depending on your circumstances and available financial resources. A further extension of up to two years may be possible under specific employment-related conditions.


### Can I work in Germany with the Opportunity Card?


Yes. You can work part-time for a combined maximum of 20 hours per week and undertake qualifying work trials of up to two weeks per employer. For regular full-time employment, you'll generally need an appropriate employment residence permit.


### How do I show proof of funds for the Germany Opportunity Card?


You can demonstrate financial resources through a blocked account, an accepted declaration of commitment or qualifying part-time employment income. In 2026, the monthly financial requirement is €1,091.
